page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor, the instance features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, supported by a cache hierarchy that includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. The architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place the n4-standard-8 in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1770.0 and a multi-core score of 6838.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 11489.89. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate solid performance with 530.44 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, though uncached large-block reads drop to 61.33 GB/sec. Notable performance limitations exist, particularly in memory-intensive and multi-threaded decompression tasks; the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25%, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is relatively weak at 36.22 GB/sec. Furthermore, while prompt processing for a 7B LLM model reaches 49.59 tokens/sec, text generation for the same model is poor, yielding only 6.31 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for mainstream workloads that do not require specialized hardware. Its dedicated CPU allocation and standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio make it a reliable option for general-purpose applications, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations. However, workloads requiring high-speed local storage, massive memory bandwidth, or heavy multi-threaded decompression may find the hardware profile restrictive. It is best suited for web serving, application hosting, CI/CD pipelines, and lightweight database tasks.
